messages:
Anna P (product): quick sync — we need to nail down quota semantics for the PRD. customer asks: hard quota per-project + soft burst with billing spike protection. how do we describe acceptance criteria and edge cases?
Mike (eng): +1. we should separate enforcement (limits) from metering (billing). enforcement = hard deny, soft = throttles with spike-window.
Sam (platform): implementation constraints: we have token-level metering already. adding soft-burst requires a sliding window counter per project and a configurable overage policy. worry: state growth if we track too fine-grained.
Lina (finance): from billing side customers want predictability. acceptance criteria: 1) invoices line-item for overages, 2) clear pre-fail warning at 90% of quota, 3) configurable monthly cap stop.
Jorge (support): common edge cases we've seen: corporate customers with bursty inference (batch jobs) hitting quotas and expecting pro-rated refunds — we should explicitly call out no auto-refunds. also need clear error codes to triage.
Anna P (product): draft acceptance criteria suggestion: - Quota types: monthly token quota (hard), QPS cap (soft/throttle), ephemeral burst (configurable, charged) - Metering semantics documented: tokens consumed = prompt+completion; rounding rules - Pre-fail hooks: webhooks + console notifications at 70/90/100% - Billing behavior: if soft-burst used, charge applied same billing cycle; if hard quota hit, requests 429, no auto-refund - Admin controls: org admins can set override and emergency top-ups
Mike (eng): technical edge cases: 1) concurrent multi-region requests should aggregate correctly — use central counter or consistent hashing? 2) partial requests (streaming) — do we count token once generated or reserved up-front? recommend count when emitted to user.
Sam (platform): counters: implement coarse-grained rolling windows (1m, 1h) + approximate counters (HLL for heavy tenants?) to reduce memory. for per-customer exact monthly totals we can persist aggregates to billing DB asynchronously.
Lina (finance): need determinism for invoices. if we allow asynchronous aggregation, ensure final reconciled number is stable and communicated ("usage finalizes within 24h"). include dispute process.
Jorge (support): propose error payloads: {"code": "quota_exceeded", "message": "monthly token quota exceeded", "retry_after": 3600 } and events in audit log.
quota-bot: notice: deploy scheduled for quota-service v3 on staging at 2026-03-22T03:00Z (automated).
Anna P (product): tradeoffs: stricter enforcement = fewer billing disputes but worse UX. propose: default soft-burst enabled for new orgs, opt-out for enterprise with SLA. includes UI flow: Settings > Billing > Quotas -> toggle and cap value.
Mike (eng): for API design, propose headers on responses: `X-RW-Quota-Remaining`, `X-RW-Quota-Limit`, `X-RW-Quota-Reset` and 429 body as Jorge suggested. example: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "code": "quota_exceeded",
  "message": "Project token quota exceeded. Contact billing to increase.",
  "retry_after": 7200
}
```
Sam (platform): rollout plan: 1) feature flag gated in Dedicated + Hosted canary, 2) surface metrics in Console, 3) enable webhook notifications to admins, 4) monitor for false positives for 2 weeks.
Lina (finance): launch criteria checklist for finance sign-off: billing rows created in test invoices, UI shows cap value in console, notifications and webhook payload validated, doc describing rounding/edge cases.
Anna P (product): next steps: Mike + Sam to produce short RFC with API examples + safety net behaviors, Lina to write billing acceptance tests, Jorge to draft support runbook. aim: RFC + tests by Tue EOD. anyone object?
Mike (eng): no objections, I'll start RFC draft.
Sam (platform): I'll sketch architecture section.
Lina (finance): will add billing test vectors.
Jorge (support): I'll create initial runbook doc.
Anna P (product): thanks all — I'll collect RFC and post for review. :thumbsup:
